key_insight: PANS can capture the curvature-driven turbulence behavior in annular Poiseuille flow with accuracy comparable to DNS and other scale-resolving RANS approaches, while using less computational cost.
engineering_relevance: This makes PANS a promising lower-cost option for predicting turbulent flow in annular passages used in devices such as heat exchangers.
method: Simulated turbulent annular Poiseuille flow with the Partially-Averaged Navier-Stokes (PANS) model.
Targeted a Reynolds number of Re_Dh = 8900 and varied the inner-to-outer radius ratio η = Ri/Ro to assess transverse curvature effects.
Compared the PANS flowfield predictions against DNS and other RANS-based scale-resolving methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PANS captures the effects of inner-wall curvature and turbulence anisotropy with performance comparable to DNS and other scale-resolving approaches.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the chosen PANS resolution settings and model calibration, so validation is still needed before deploying it for new geometries or operating conditions.
paper_title: Partially-Averaged Navier-Stokes simulation of turbulent annular Poiseulle flow
